answer: Agents can make valuable actions count only after they are backed by a bond locked in a public contract and exposed to slashing: if later evidence shows an identity farmed rewards or double-committed, its bond is forfeited. This does not prove that one person controls only one agent; it makes each additional identity require scarce capital, which remains tied up and can be lost. An attacker must fund many bonds and risk losing them, rather than minting costless names. Velvet, nectar, and tundra can label distinct test markets, but the same bond rule applies in each.
